- Detect explicit fix intent on initial PR `/orchestrate` requests, including merge-conflict, rebase, and direct "fix this PR" wording.
- Dispatch those requests to `fix-pr` with request-specific handoff context instead of starting with `review`.
- Update orchestrator docs for deterministic PR routing.

## Verification

- `npm run build`
- `git diff --check`
- `node --test .agent/dist/__tests__/orchestrate-handoff-cli.test.js`

Closes #179

> Dual-agent review by **Claude** and **Codex**.
> Requested by @lolipopshock.

## Summary of PR/Issue
- PR #181 addresses issue #179, where initial PR `/orchestrate` ignored explicit fix intent and routed to `review`.
- The PR adds deterministic request-text detection so merge-conflict, rebase, and direct “fix this PR” wording dispatches `fix-pr`.
- It also adds request-specific handoff context, regression coverage for two positive cases, and docs updates for deterministic PR routing.
- The overall design fits the linked issue: keep PR `/orchestrate` deterministic rather than moving it through the planner.

## Review
- No BLOCKING findings. The implementation is directionally correct, but two routing edge cases should be fixed before merge.
- The main risks are false-positive fix intent detection and loss of the explicit request when `CHANGES_REQUESTED` takes precedence.

| Issue | Severity | Description |
| -- | -- | -- |
| Intent detector can misroute review-only text to fix-pr | WARNING | Bare `rebase` and ambiguous `fix it/this/that` matches can route review/question phrasing into a write-capable `fix-pr` pass. Narrow the patterns and add negative coverage. |
| Explicit fix requests lose handoff context when CHANGES_REQUESTED | WARNING | The `CHANGES_REQUESTED` branch runs before the explicit-fix branch, so combined cases dispatch `fix-pr` with generic requested-change context instead of the user’s request. |
| Technical docs omit the new explicit-fix context variant | INFO | The routing docs were updated, but the later handoff-context paragraph still only describes review-synthesis and `CHANGES_REQUESTED` manual PR contexts. |

## Progress
- Existing PR discussion and inline comments were checked before posting; there were no prior inline comments to deduplicate.
- Posted 2 new inline comments on `.agent/src/cli/orchestrate-handoff.ts`: line 938 for false-positive intent matching and line 1309 for `CHANGES_REQUESTED` precedence.
- No inline replies were added and no comments were minimized.
- Rubrics review passed and found no rubric-specific issues.

## Issue Details

<details>
<summary>Intent detector can misroute review-only text to fix-pr</summary>

**Cause:** In [`orchestrate-handoff.ts`](https://github.com/self-evolving/repo/blob/f61c895c55367502d755421823f02122a44256aa/.agent/src/cli/orchestrate-handoff.ts#L938), `\brebase\b` matches any rebase mention, and the later `fix it/this/that` pattern lacks a PR/branch referent. That can classify “please review whether a rebase is needed” as explicit fix intent.

**Candidate solutions:** Require imperative phrasing for rebase-related routing, drop or constrain `fix it/this/that`, and add negative tests for non-fix request text on open PRs.

**Comments:** Claude and Codex both flagged the false-positive surface, with slightly different examples.

</details>

<details>
<summary>Explicit fix requests lose handoff context when CHANGES_REQUESTED</summary>

**Cause:** In [`orchestrate-handoff.ts`](https://github.com/self-evolving/repo/blob/f61c895c55367502d755421823f02122a44256aa/.agent/src/cli/orchestrate-handoff.ts#L1309), explicit fix intent is checked after `CHANGES_REQUESTED`. When both are true, the earlier branch dispatches `fix-pr` without `manualPrExplicitFixHandoffContext()`, so fallback context tells `fix-pr` to address generic requested-change comments.

**Candidate solutions:** Check explicit fix intent before `CHANGES_REQUESTED`, or merge the original request into the `CHANGES_REQUESTED` handoff context when both apply. Add a regression test for the combined case.

**Comments:** One reviewer treated this as INFO/out of scope, while another raised it to WARNING because `fix-pr` treats `ORCHESTRATOR_CONTEXT` as the selected task.

</details>

<details>
<summary>Technical docs omit the new explicit-fix context variant</summary>

**Cause:** [`agent-orchestrator.md`](https://github.com/self-evolving/repo/blob/f61c895c55367502d755421823f02122a44256aa/.agent/docs/technical-details/agent-orchestrator.md#L152) still describes only review-originated context and manual PR `CHANGES_REQUESTED` context, not the new explicit fix-intent context.

**Candidate solutions:** Add one sentence noting that manual PR `/orchestrate` starts with explicit fix intent pass the original request as the selected `fix-pr` task.

</details>

## Recommended Next Step
FIX_PR: The remaining warnings are concrete branch changes with clear tests and are safe for an automated fix-pr pass.

## Final Verdict
MINOR_ISSUES

## Action Items
- [ ] Narrow explicit fix-intent matching so review/question phrasing around `rebase` or ambiguous `fix it/this/that` does not route to `fix-pr`, and add negative regression coverage.
- [ ] Preserve request-specific handoff context when a PR has both `CHANGES_REQUESTED` and explicit fix intent, with a regression test for the combined case.

@sepo-agent /answer ok can u summarize why starting from the initial version it got changed so much

Short version: it grew because the first implementation fixed the happy path, but review found that the routing rule controls a write-capable `fix-pr` workflow, so the matcher had to be much more careful.

What changed after the initial version:

- The original issue was narrow: PR `/orchestrate` was always starting with `review` unless the PR already had `CHANGES_REQUESTED`, even when the user explicitly said “merge conflict ... fix.” See #179’s diagnosis: https://github.com/self-evolving/repo/issues/179#issuecomment-4410671279
- The first PR version added explicit fix-intent detection and routed those PR comments to `fix-pr`.
- Review then caught that the first matcher was too broad: words like `rebase`, `merge conflict`, or `fix this` could accidentally route review-only/advice requests into `fix-pr`.
- Review also caught that if a PR already had `CHANGES_REQUESTED`, the new explicit user request could get swallowed by the older generic requested-changes path.
- The follow-up commits tightened the matcher to handle negated/self-directed/review-only wording like “do not fix this PR,” “tell me what to fix,” and “review whether a rebase is needed,” while still accepting explicit asks like “could you please rebase this PR.”
- Most of the extra size is regression coverage: the tests now cover positive fix requests, negative false-positive cases, and the `CHANGES_REQUESTED` overlap.

The final shape is still the same narrow feature: deterministic PR `/orchestrate` routing. It just became safer. Hmmm so do we do this detection for an agent based route since the model should be able to parse this intent? And the changes here are mostly adding support for heuristic route? Is it correct? @sepo-agent /answer

Yes, that’s basically right: this PR is adding a deterministic/heuristic route for one specific PR `/orchestrate` case.

The important nuance is that `agent` mode currently does **not** mean “the model decides every initial route.” The current dispatcher only sends **issue-level** initial `/orchestrate` through the planner in agent mode. PR-level initial `/orchestrate` still goes through `decideManualOrchestration()`, which is deterministic: `CHANGES_REQUESTED -> fix-pr`, otherwise `review`.

So the PR is correct **if we want to preserve that architecture**:

- PR `/orchestrate` remains predictable and auditable.
- The model still handles the actual `fix-pr` work after dispatch.
- The deterministic layer only decides whether the first workflow should be `review` or `fix-pr`.
- Because `fix-pr` can write to the branch, the heuristic has to be conservative.

But your instinct is also right: if we want “agent-based route” to mean the model should parse intent for PR starts too, then this is not the ideal long-term shape. In that design, PR `/orchestrate` would call the planner with a strict schema like `review | fix-pr | answer | stop`, then policy gates would validate the selected route before dispatch.

I’d frame this PR as a narrow patch, not a general intent system. It fixes the known bug without changing orchestration architecture. If we see this matcher keep growing, that’s the signal to replace PR-start heuristics with planner-based routing instead of adding more regex cases.

title: Route PR orchestrate fix intent to fix-pr
